overview.text: Spirited Away (Japanese title: Sen to Chihiro no Kamikakushi) is a 2001 Japanese animated fantasy film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki for Studio Ghibli. Ten-year-old Chihiro enters a spirit world with her parents; after they are transformed into pigs, she takes a job in a bathhouse for spirits and tries to save them. The bathhouse, filled with unusual beings including a dragon and a witch, gives the film its distinctive setting. Chihiro’s efforts to adapt and act courageously make it a coming-of-age story. The film won the Academy Award for Animated Feature at the 2003 ceremony, a major international recognition for the work.

key_facts.text: Studio Ghibli lists the Japanese release date as July 20, 2001, and the running time as about 125 minutes.
Joe Hisaishi composed the film’s music.
Chihiro’s parents become pigs, and she finds work in a bathhouse while trying to rescue them.
The Academy records Spirited Away as the Animated Feature winner at the 75th Academy Awards ceremony in 2003.
The film’s spirit-world adventure includes encounters with a dragon and a witch.
